newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech FinMin sees fx reserves down in '97 - agency.
newsitem.headline: Czech FinMin sees fx reserves down in '97 - agency.

text.p: The Czech Republic's foreign reserves will drop by $400 million in 1997, Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik was quoted as saying by the local CTK news agency on Friday.
"In the next year, the total foreign reserves of the Czech Republic will drop by $400 million," Kocarnik said.
Reserves at the central bank as of the end of July stood at $12.97 billion, up from $10.1 billion a year ago.
Kocarnik said the current account will end up with a $3.4 billion deficit, while the capital account should end up with a surplus of $3 billion.
"The difference between the two figures represents the changes in the total foreign reserves," he said, giving no further details.
The Czech current account deficit for the first half of 1996 rose to $1.7 billion compared with a deficit of $723 million for the first half of 1995.
The capital account posted a surplus for the first six months of $800.8 million compared with a surplus of $3.1 billion in the same period last year.
